title: Alash Autonomy
capsule: The Alash Autonomy was proclaimed on 13 December 1917 at the Second All-Kazakh Congress in Orenburg, establishing a provisional Kazakh government — the Alash Orda — led by the liberal intellectual Alikhan Bukeikhanov in response to the Bolshevik seizure of power. The autonomy encompassed the Kazakh steppe regions of the former Russian empire and initially aligned with anti-Bolshevik White forces, though it never received international recognition. As White Army fortunes collapsed in 1919, Alash Orda leaders negotiated with the Bolsheviks, and Soviet forces occupied Kazakhstan through 1920. The autonomy was formally dissolved on 26 August 1920 when the Kirghiz (Kazakh) Autonomous Soviet Socialist Republic was proclaimed, absorbing its territory; Bukeikhanov and other Alash leaders were eventually arrested and shot during the 1937 purges.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The political existence and leadership are well-documented; the precise territorial boundaries claimed by Alash Orda on the steppe are approximate, as effective control was contested throughout.
